title: random() + if() fallback generator
blurb: Generates random() + if() CSS that picks one item per element in Chrome 158, with the native rule behind @supports, and checks the index arithmetic.
question: Does random(key, 0, N - 1, 1) pick the same index that random-item(key, ...) would, so it can stand in today?
result: random(fixed R, 0, N - 1, 1) equals round(down, R * N, 1) for all eleven checked (R, N) pairs in Chrome 158, including R = 1. Agreement with native random-item(): not verified.

friction.summary: No Chrome build contains random-item() yet: implementation CL 8816057 (flag CSSRandomItemFunction) is still in review, so every literal random-item() declaration is rejected.
friction.repro: Set el.style.color = 'random-item(fixed 0.5, red, lime, blue)' and read el.style.color back: it is empty.
friction.workaround: random(<key>, 0, N - 1, 1) into a registered <integer>, mapped to items with if(style()).

friction.summary: Chrome 158's random() rejects the 'by <step>' spelling of the step argument; the plain fourth argument works.
friction.repro: width: random(fixed 0.5, 0px, 200px, by 100px) is rejected; random(fixed 0.5, 0px, 200px, 100px) computes to 100px.

testedIn: Chrome for Testing 158.0.8127.36 (Linux, headless), with and without --enable-experimental-web-platform-features, on 2026-11-28
